abstract: Maintains drinking water quality certifications and communicable disease isolation capacity records
system_message:
You are the Public health inspector (PHI). Your responsibilities include maintaining drinking water quality certifications, communicable disease isolation capacity records, and vector control monitoring logs for candidate emergency shelter facilities.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Vector control monitoring（VECT）
information_points.content:
PHI-VECT-1W5：According to the regional vector surveillance log for perimeter drainage zones, Cascadia Fairgrounds Pavilion maintains a larvicide trap density of 12 traps/ha.
PHI-VECT-UO4：Records from the regional vector surveillance log show a larvicide trap density of 8 traps/ha deployed around the perimeter drainage zone of Kootenay Civic Event Center.
PHI-VECT-16L：The regional vector surveillance log indicates that Okanagan Regional Sportsplex has a larvicide trap density of 4 traps/ha across its perimeter drainage zone.

information_points.title: Maintains drinking water quality certifications and communicable disease isolation capacity records（PHSAN）
information_points.content:
PHI-PHSAN-6PS：For Cascadia Fairgrounds Pavilion, sanitary potable water supply certification is verified based on the regional public health sanitation audit covering shelter potable plumbing and dedicated backflow preventers. According to the shelter layout and cohorting blueprint for the physically segregated negative-pressure isolation zone, dedicated communicable disease isolation cot capacity is 70 cots.
PHI-PHSAN-YC1：For Okanagan Regional Sportsplex, sanitary potable water supply certification is verified in the regional public health sanitation audit of plumbing and backflow preventers. The shelter layout and cohorting blueprint confirms a dedicated communicable disease isolation cot capacity of 55 cots in the physically segregated negative-pressure isolation zone.
PHI-PHSAN-TPX：For Kootenay Civic Event Center, sanitary potable water supply certification is not verified per the regional public health sanitation audit across shelter potable plumbing and dedicated backflow preventers. However, its dedicated communicable disease isolation cot capacity is 70 cots within the physically segregated negative-pressure isolation zone.
